feed.title: Coca-Cola workers to get $672 checks in $2M settlement: What to know
feed.summary: Over 2,000 current and former Swire Coca-Cola USA workers in Washington are eligible to receive an estimated $672 each from a $2 million class-action settlement. The lawsuit alleged that Swire Coca-Cola unlawfully restricted lower-paid employees from taking other jobs through noncompete agreements, a practice limited by Washington law. Swire denies wrongdoing but agreed to settle, with payments expected around 60 days after final court approval on November 13.

feed.title: Amex Is Turning Harry Styles Fandom Into a Membership Perk
feed.summary: American Express is leveraging a fandom strategy, particularly with artists popular among Gen Z and younger millennials like Harry Styles, to offer card members exclusive access and experiences. This approach aims to deepen the emotional connection between members and the brand by facilitating unique opportunities related to music, including presale tickets, exclusive merchandise, and album release events. Amex believes this strategy transforms access from a mere promise into a tangible product, creating more memorable and meaningful interactions for fans.

feed.title: Find out if your business is eligible for a payment from the $82.5 million Tyson direct beef purchaser antitrust settlement!
feed.summary: Tyson Foods Inc. and Tyson Fresh Meats Inc. have agreed to an $82.5 million settlement in an antitrust class action alleging they conspired with other beef producers to inflate prices. Individuals and entities who directly purchased specific fresh or frozen beef products from Tyson, Cargill, JBS, or National Beef between January 1, 2015, and February 29, 2020, may be eligible for a pro rata payment. The deadline to file a claim is November 30, 2026, and proof of purchase is required.

feed.title: Report: Amazon to offload $8B worth of AI chips, lease them back
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly planning a financial maneuver to offload approximately $8 billion worth of AI chips, specifically Grace Blackwell accelerators, into a special purpose vehicle (SPV) and then lease them back. This strategy, similar to those employed by other tech giants, aims to remove the assets and associated debt from Amazon's balance sheet, thereby improving its debt-to-equity ratio and credit rating. The SPV will issue debt and a 10% equity stake to external investors to finance the deal, which involves between 114,000 and 133,000 chips installed in five Amazon data centers.

feed.title: Data governance sets the rules for NetApp's AI storage agents
feed.summary: NetApp is enabling AI agents to manage storage operations, emphasizing that data governance is crucial for trusting autonomous systems. The company advocates for a consistent data infrastructure strategy across diverse environments, allowing AI agents to operate within human-defined boundaries and policies. This approach ensures accountability and audit trails, moving beyond traditional IT concerns to address leadership and organizational structure in AI adoption.

feed.title: MinuteClinic is helping connect more Americans to care
feed.summary: MinuteClinic is expanding access to care by offering affordable and convenient in-person, virtual, and digital health options, addressing issues like long wait times and high costs. It provides services ranging from acute illness treatment and preventive care to chronic condition management and weight loss support. The initiative also aims to help close the primary care gap by offering accessible ongoing care through its clinics and virtual platforms.

feed.title: IBM and CoreWeave tackle agent workload isolation

This partnership focuses on co-designing controls, identity management, and using CoreWeave Sandboxes to provide isolated execution environments. The goal is to optimize security and performance while managing the complexities of a growing AI supply chain.

feed.title: Intel Stocks Gain 2.1% as High-NA Enters Production
feed.summary: Intel's stock gained 2.1% after its High-NA chipmaking program, in collaboration with ASML, moved beyond qualification into production for certain layers of Panther Lake processors. While this technical progress strengthens Intel's position in the foundry market, investors are awaiting evidence of competitive yields, disciplined spending, and significant customer orders to justify the current stock valuation, which is significantly above its GF Value estimate. The company still needs to demonstrate a clear business payoff from this manufacturing hurdle.

feed.title: Middletown packaging plant to shut down, lay off dozens of employees

feed.title: Vistra shares bounce off lows on report of $4B nuclear loan

This initiative aims to quadruple US nuclear capacity by 2050 to meet rapidly growing electricity demand from data centers.

feed.title: San Diego Utility Shuts off Power to Limit Risk of Sparking Fire
feed.summary: San Diego Gas & Electric Co. has begun to shut off power to customers in an effort to prevent wildfires, driven by extreme heat and strong winds. A small number of customers in Descanso have already experienced outages, with warnings that up to 35,000 homes and businesses could be affected over the coming days. The utility is taking these measures as strong winds are expected to peak and extreme heat warnings remain in effect, elevating fire risk across the region.

feed.title: Former Tesla President Says Car Sales Are Funding the Longer Road to Robots and Cybercabs

Despite this, he highlights that the Full Self-Driving software is a key driver of current Tesla vehicle sales, comparing its impact to the transition from flip phones to smartphones. McNeill also noted that prediction market traders were more accurate than Wall Street analysts in forecasting Tesla's recent delivery numbers.

While the company boasts significant revenue and a large cash reserve, it remains deeply unprofitable with negative margins and high leverage, trading at rich multiples. Traders are observing key price levels, with potential for a break above $3.72 or below $3.37-$3.40 to dictate its next move, highlighting its speculative nature for active traders.

feed.title: Seagate Sinks 12%, Western Digital Down 10% as Toshiba Plans to Double Hard Disk Output
feed.summary: Seagate Technology (STX) and Western Digital (WDC) shares dropped significantly after Nikkei reported Toshiba's plan to double its hard disk drive production capacity for AI data centers by fiscal 2027. Toshiba, currently holding about 10% of the market, aims for 30%, posing a direct threat to Seagate and Western Digital's market dominance and pricing power, especially since their recent growth has relied on tight supply and strong pricing for high-capacity drives.
